newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rain may delay maize harvest in France's southwest.
newsitem.headline: Rain may delay maize harvest in France's southwest.

text.p: Rain and cool temperatures threaten to push back the start of the bulk of maize harvest in parts of France's southwest, crop analysts said on Monday.
But in eastern France, dry weather has allowed combining of early variety maize to begin, they said.
In the Aquitaine region, the country's number one maize producer, combining of early variety maize started in early September on the sandy patches of the Hautes-Landes and is now 20 percent complete.
But steady rain and cold weather may delay the start of the bulk of the harvest by about a week. The harvest traditionally gets in full swing in early October in the region.

"The crop potential is good but weather conditions are far from ideal. We need some sun over the next week to allow the grain to fully mature," said one analyst for the local ONIC grain office in Bordeaux.

Local ONIC officials said they they were maintaining their forecast of 1996 yields at the 1993 record of 8.6 tonnes per hectare after 8.0 tonnes last year. Maize area is expected to rise 4.2 percent to 370,000 hectares.
In the Midi-Pyrenees region local ONIC officials in Toulouse said they were not yet concerned over possible delays as the bulk of harvest starts only in mid-October.
They put the local yield for 1996 at the 1993 record of 7.8 tonnes against 7.2 tonnes last year. Area is seen rising 4.6 percent to 225,000 hectares.
In eastern France the first maize cuttings started over the weekend in Alsace.
Local yields are expected to jump to 9.5 tonnes per hectare from 8.9 tonnes and area to 126,000 hectares from 115,000 hectares.
The French maize growers association, AGPM, has put the national crop at 13.8 million tonnes, up one million tonnes from 1995.
